reading_rule: Method context and limitations only. These sources do not validate the new 10 km model or its assumed hub stiffness. The implementation is independently derived and checked against analytic identities.

sources.title: Parametric Studies of Square Solar Sails Using Finite Element Analysis
sources.authors: David W. Sleight and Danniella M. Muheim
sources.read_scope: NTRS abstract and retrieved PDF passages on pretension, inertia relief, mesh convergence and eigenanalysis; not a complete scholarly review.
sources.supports: Full sail models couple membrane and boom properties, use nonlinear pretension and inertia relief, and check mesh-dependent displacement and frequencies.
sources.limits: Their nonlinear models are substantially richer than this prescribed-prestress, normal-only energy model; reported numerical frequencies are not experimental validation of our construction. The abstract flags nonphysical modes associated with omitted wrinkling.

sources.title: The nodal-based floating frame of reference formulation with modal reduction
sources.read_scope: Open article abstract, introduction and derivation through equations 17; extracted text of modal-reduction context. Not a complete reproduction of the paper.
sources.supports: Separating large rigid motion from small relative elastic deformation requires consistent kinetic energy and inertial coupling. Modal reduction and nodal kinematics are appropriate implementation tools.
sources.limits: The paper develops a consistent-mass treatment; our mass is deliberately lumped and therefore retains the approximation cautioned about in this source. The support endpoint approximation does not reproduce exact frame inertia.

sources.title: Finite Element Analysis and Test Correlation of a 10-Meter Inflation-Deployed Solar Sail
sources.read_scope: Indexed NTRS abstract and metadata, plus retrieved PDF excerpt describing 10 m sail model ingredients. Direct page/PDF opens failed; this is not a full paper reading.
sources.supports: Ground-test analysis used membrane or shell elements, boom/spreader beams, cable or truss elements, and measured concentrated masses.
sources.limits: No numerical test result from this source is adopted. It motivates treating membrane, support and attached mass separately; it does not establish our compliance or scale extrapolation.
sources.authors: Sleight, Michii, Lichodziejewski, Derbès, Mann, Slade and Wang
sources.access_note: The full PDF opened in the source check of 14 October 2026; its model description matches the excerpt.

new_model_assumptions: Uniform prescribed isotropic membrane tension and circular-edge cable tension are taken from the prior support product.
Linear triangle gradient energy and cable transverse slope energy act relative to the hub best-fit plane; this enforces affine normal rigid-motion invariance.
Four radial-boom endpoint compliances use inherited cantilever bending and web shear, including its declared amplification factor.
Hub twist stiffness is four times one inherited member reciprocal tip compliance: an uncalibrated effective restraint, not a solved frame eigenmodel.
Film mass is triangle-lumped and normalized to the analytic curved area; support masses are endpoint-lumped, preserving mass and centre of mass but not exact distributed-frame inertia.
Modal eigenproblems and analytic checks verify the stated model, not prestress realizability, nonlinear deformation, damage tolerance or flight performance.
